data_condition_or_issue_raw: Unfiltered repository corpora contain deprecated API usages alongside replacements.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Training intent-test pairs can be irrelevant to the focal method.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Training tests have low branch coverage and provide little evidence about conditional paths.
data_operation_or_comparison: Compare original, syntax-only, syntax+relevance, and all-filtered datasets including the coverage filter.
generated_outcome_raw: Generated tests cover more paths and detect more real bugs when high-coverage examples are retained.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Unit-test training pairs include focal methods with empty catch/finally blocks, so exceptions are caught but not handled.
data_operation_or_comparison: CleanTest's syntactic filter removes such pairs as one of several syntax-noise rules; models are fine-tuned on original versus filtered datasets.
generated_outcome_raw: Generated tests may miss exception behavior in the noisy condition, whereas filtered-data tests cover boundary and extreme cases more comprehensively.
outcome_measure_if_reported: Empty-exception noise occurs in 0.68% of Methods2Test and 0.56% of Atlas; the full filter improves line/branch coverage across four models and average detected bugs by 24.23%, but no empty-exception-only effect is reported.
relationship_summary: The paper links empty exception handlers in training focal methods to tests that may miss errors, removes those pairs within CleanTest, and reports more boundary-aware generated tests after bundled cleaning.
evidence_section: 2.2 Taxonomy of Noise Data; 3.1 Rule-based Syntactic Filter; 4.4-5.1 Results
evidence_locator: paper.txt lines 263-281, 475-477, 670-782, and 839-912; unique phrases 'exceptions are caught but not handled' and 'boundary conditions and extreme cases'.
notes: The syntactic filter also removes ambiguous types, annotations, empty functions, syntax errors, and non-English literals; count this as a reported association within a bundled intervention, not an isolated robustness effect. Boundary coverage and bug detection are coded as generated-test Correctness, not as stability of the generated test itself.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Optimal human solutions are a minority while non-optimal implementations are more frequent in LLM training data.
data_operation_or_comparison: Measure generated-code runtime and memory, then provide an author explanation; no corpus inspection or retraining comparison.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Training corpora are hypothesized to vary in the abundance and variety of efficient examples across algorithm families.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Efficiency-oriented training labels use the fastest correct solution for SFT and top-five fast-versus-slow solution pairs for DPO.

generated_outcome_raw: DPO generally improves generated-code efficiency while preserving or improving correctness for sufficiently large models.

relationship_summary: Training on explicit fast-versus-slow solution preferences steers larger code models toward more efficient correct code.
evidence_locator: paper.txt lines 249-270 and 289-315; unique phrase 'select the top 5 pairs of solutions that exhibit the most significant discrepancy in runtime'
notes: Data construction and DPO optimization are inseparable; likely a new/retargeted Efficiency-to-Efficiency relationship.

data_condition_or_issue_raw: Public code training corpora plausibly contain simple single-statement bugs that persist in repositories.
